paper.title: Aging Bandits: Regret Analysis and Order-Optimal Learning Algorithm for Wireless Networks with Stochastic Arrivals

settings.name_in_paper: Aging Bandit problem with queue-independent channel policies
unmapped: Arms are N wireless channels with i.i.d. Bernoulli ON/OFF states (unknown reliabilities mu_n); the cost is the Age-of-Information of M sources, which is history-dependent (depends on past deliveries and packet generations)
M sources generate packets as i.i.d. Bernoulli(lambda) processes with known lambda in (0,1); learner also selects a source (work-conserving source policy)
AoI regret: expected cumulative AoI difference to a genie algorithm using the optimal source policy and the best channel
Channel policy does not observe queue status (queue-independent)
Assumes the optimal source policy is the same irrespective of the channel policy
settings.definition_quote: At every time slot, the learning algorithm selects a single pair (source, channel) and the selected source attempts to transmit its packet via the selected channel. ... The AoI regret ... R^\pi(T) = E[ sum_m sum_t h^\pi_m(t) - sum_m sum_t h^*_m(t) ]

settings.name_in_paper: Aging Bandit problem with queue-dependent channel policies (E(t) observed)
unmapped: Arms are N wireless channels with i.i.d. Bernoulli ON/OFF states; cost is history-dependent Age-of-Information of M sources with Bernoulli(lambda) packet arrivals, lambda in (0,1) known
Channel policy observes whether the system is empty E(t) and can transmit dummy packets (free exploration) when empty
AoI regret against genie with optimal source policy and best channel
Assumes the optimal source policy is the same irrespective of the channel policy
settings.definition_quote: we develop a learning algorithm \bar\eta\in\bar\Pi with a queue-dependent channel policy that selects n(t) using information about the outcome of previous transmission attempts ... and about the current status of the transmission queues, E(t).

algorithms.name: Any learning algorithm in Pi* (optimal source policy + queue-independent channel policy)

symbols.EK_T: expected number of suboptimal channel choices E[K^pi(T)] of the algorithm

conditions: any learning algorithm pi in Pi (any work-conserving source policy and any queue-independent channel policy)

source.label: p1
source.quote: For any given network configuration $(\lambda,\vec\mu)$, the AoI regret of any learning algorithm $\pi\in\Pi$ scales at least on the order of its expected number of suboptimal channel choices, namely $R^\pi(T) = \Omega\left( \mathrm{E}\left[ K^{\pi}(T) \right] \right)$.

results.notes: Quantity is AoI regret (expected cumulative AoI difference to genie), recorded as 'other'. Proof only outlined. Combined with Prop 3 gives Corollary 4: Theta(E[K]) for pi in Pi*.

symbols.EK_T: expected number of suboptimal channel choices E[K^pi(T)] of the algorithm

conditions: algorithm uses the optimal source policy pi_a^* (class Pi*)

source.label: t2
source.quote: For any given network configuration $(\lambda,\vec\mu)$, the AoI regret of any learning algorithm $\pi\in\Pi^*$ scales at most on the order of its expected number of suboptimal channel choices, namely $R^\pi(T) = O\left( \mathrm{E}\left[ K^{\pi}(T) \right] \right)$.

results.notes: Generic reduction. Text (not a formal statement) concludes epsilon-Greedy, UCB, TS channel policies have AoI regret Theta(log T).

conditions: any learning algorithm pi in Pi that is alpha-consistent (E[T_n(T)] = O(T^alpha) for all suboptimal channels in every configuration)

source.label: r2
source.quote: In \cite[Corollary~$20$]{RegretQueueing}, the authors show that any learning algorithm $\pi\in\Pi$ that is $\alpha$-consistent has an expected number of suboptimal channel choices that scales as $E\left[ K^{\pi}(T) \right] = \Omega(\log T)$ ... Hence, it follows from the lower bound in Proposition~\ref{p1} that the associated AoI regret scales as $R^\pi(T) = \Omega(\log T)$

results.notes: Derived by combining a cited result (Krishnasamy et al.) with Proposition 2.

source.label: t3
source.quote: For any given network configuration $(\lambda,\vec\mu)$, the AoI regret of the order-optimal learning algorithm $\bar\eta$ is bounded, namely $R^{\bar\eta}(T)=O(1)$.

results.notes: Proof gives R <= C_y M C_p with C_p <= 2(N-1)/(exp(1/(2N^2))-1) + 2(N-1)/(exp(Delta_min^2/(4N))-1); C_y unspecified constant. Algorithm uses optimal source policy (not characterised) so compute marked polynomial only for channel policy. Algorithm does not use T.
